verdict.verdict: No meaningful gain: clinical detail (stage, comorbidities) adds nothing even inside Synthea; Synthea-derived scores give the MEPS model at most a tiny Brier gain (about -0.001) and no clear AUROC gain. But a Synthea model on shared variables alone ranks real survivors about as well as the survey model (tie within CI)
verdict.detail: (1) Inside Synthea (660 synthetic patients, 4033 person-years), clinical-only features (stage, metastasis, comorbidities, opioids, kidney function) add no signal over shared variables: AUROC 0.671 -> 0.670, d -0.001 [-0.008, +0.007]; stage is missing in 86% of person-years. (2) A Synthea model on shared variables only, applied unchanged to real MEPS survivors, ranks them at AUROC 0.686 [0.634, 0.740] with O/E 1.02, vs the MEPS model's 0.666 out-of-fold (paired d +0.020 [-0.021, +0.063]): the shared-variable risk pattern learned from synthetic records transports about as well as a model fit on the survey itself. (3) Added to the MEPS model: clinical-burden score d AUROC +0.004 [-0.003, +0.012], d Brier -0.0012 [-0.0022, -0.0001]; Synthea prior d AUROC +0.004 [-0.002, +0.010], d Brier -0.0009 [-0.0018, -0.0000]; stratum features (3 definitions) d AUROC between -0.006 and -0.003. (Q3's MEPS-only reference is 0.663, not 0.666, because it uses a wider C grid.) Without a shared key every Synthea feature is a function of variables MEPS already has, so a gain means the simulation is a useful prior at n=466, not that real stage or comorbidity data would help these patients. The submission uses the MEPS-only model.

design:
Do the synthetic clinical records (Synthea) add anything beyond the MEPS survey?

Usage: .venv/bin/python -I analysis/synthea.py [data]     (expects data/meps and data/synthea; run train.py first)
Writes analysis/out/synthea.json.

There is no key between MEPS and Synthea, so no individual can be linked. Three pre-registered questions:
  Q1 (inside Synthea): do clinical-only features (stage, comorbidities, metastasis, opioids, kidney function)
     add AUROC over the features both sources share? Person-years, CV grouped by patient.
     Pass: paired dAUROC 95% CI above 0.
  Q2 (transport): a Synthea model trained on shared features only, applied unchanged to MEPS dev survivors.
     Pass: AUROC CI above 0.5. Also reports calibration (O/E) to show the population shift.
  Q3 (increment in MEPS): add Synthea-derived features to the MEPS model, same repeated CV as train.py,
     paired against MEPS-only. (a) transferred "clinical burden" score = E[clinical part of the Synthea logit |
     shared features]; (b) shrunken stratum features (acute rate, advanced-stage share, comorbidity burden)
     under three stratum definitions. Pass: dAUROC CI above 0 or dBrier CI below 0.
Only MEPS survivors with breast, colon, lung or prostate cancer are aligned to strata (Synthea has only those);
everyone else gets the overall Synthea mean plus an "unaligned" flag.

vsMepsModel.note: Paired bootstrap: Synthea shared-variable model (never saw MEPS) vs MEPS logistic OOF predictions, same 466 survivors.

notAligned: MEPS survivors with only skin, melanoma, uterine, cervical, bladder, lymphoma or other cancers (Synthea has none) get the overall Synthea mean and an 'unaligned' flag. Individual records were never matched: with no key, a person-level join on age/sex/race/cancer would be mostly noise.
